pairs.why: B's palm trunk and fronds are a little smoother and softer-edged, like the real tree's clean painted surface, while A's trunk rings look slightly chunkier.
B's wood has a quiet, low-contrast grain and the bands are crisp metal, whereas A has more heavily drawn, louder grain and rivets on a glossier body.
B's metal has a fuller range of matte and bright highlights with the dome as a separate gloss accent, whereas A's disc is a flat, uniform chrome.
A's bottle is a softer, more matte-satin plastic with simple highlights, similar to the real semi-translucent bottle, while B is glossier and has more lacquered specular glints.
A's clock face is smoother and its rim has a soft satin highlight like the real one, while B's rim is a flat matte orange with little sheen.
Both marble pieces have similar faint veining and a smooth matte stone finish, so material gives no reason to choose.
A's casing has smooth satin metal and rubber with a few crisp highlights, as in the real light, while B has more small gold bits and a noisier surface.
A's slide is smooth, soft molded plastic with broad highlights like the real one, while B is slightly more textured and glassy, with a busy water surface.
